name: Database Management Systems
description: Relational model, SQL queries, Normalization, ACID properties, Indexing (B-Trees), and Transactions.

topics.title: SQL Queries & Joins
topics.notes: INNER JOIN returns matching rows in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all from left + matching from right. GROUP BY is used with aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM, AVG.
keyPoints: HAVING clause filters groups after aggregation.
Subqueries can be correlated or non-correlated.

topics.title: ACID Properties & Transactions
topics.notes: Atomicity (All or nothing), Consistency (Valid state transition), Isolation (Concurrent transactions do not collide), Durability (Committed data persists).
keyPoints: Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable.

topics.title: Database Normalization
topics.notes: 1NF: Atomic values. 2NF: No partial dependency. 3NF: No transitive dependency. BCNF: For every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key.
keyPoints: Prevents Insertion, Deletion, and Update anomalies.

mcqs.question: Which of the following guarantees that a database transaction is completely executed or not executed at all?
mcqs.explanation: Atomicity ensures "all or nothing" execution of transactions.

interviewQuestions: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING clause in SQL?
Explain B-Trees and B+ Trees indexing mechanism.
What is the difference between Primary Key and Unique Key?

name: Operating Systems
description: Process management, Multithreading, CPU Scheduling, Deadlocks, Memory Management, Virtual Memory, and Paging.

topics.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
topics.notes: FCFS, SJF (Shortest Job First), Round Robin (Time quantum based), Priority Scheduling.
keyPoints: SJF gives minimum average waiting time.
Round Robin prevents starvation with proper time quantum.

topics.title: Deadlocks & Bankers Algorithm
topics.notes: 4 Necessary Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.
keyPoints: Bankers algorithm is used for Deadlock Avoidance.

interviewQuestions: Explain Paging and Thrashing in OS.
How does Semaphore differ from Mutex?

name: Computer Networks
description: OSI & TCP/IP models, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP vs UDP, IP Addressing, Subnetting, Routing Algorithms, and DNS.

topics.title: TCP vs UDP Protocols
topics.notes: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, guarantees packet delivery via 3-Way Handshake. UDP is connectionless, faster, unreliable (ideal for video streaming).
keyPoints: TCP Flow control uses Sliding Window.

interviewQuestions: What happens when you type www.google.com in your browser?
What is the role of ARP and DNS?

name: Object Oriented Programming

topics.title: SOLID Design Principles
topics.notes: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion.

interviewQuestions: What is the difference between Function Overloading and Overriding?

What is Abstract Class vs Interface?
